tool.name: CRISPRTarget
tool.description: predict the targets of CRISPR spacers in phage, plasmid or other sequence databases
tool.command:
## the spacer input, either a CRISPR array annotation or a set of spacer sequences #if str($spacer_input.input_type) == 'fasta' #if $spacer_input.spacers.is_of_type('fasta.gz') gunzip -c '$spacer_input.spacers' > spacers.fna && #else ln -s '$spacer_input.spacers' spacers.fna && #end if #else #if $spacer_input.crispr_gff.is_of_type('gff3.gz') gunzip -c '$spacer_input.crispr_gff' > spacers.gff && #else ln -s '$spacer_input.crispr_gff' spacers.gff && #end if #end if
## the target database and the shuffled database used as background for the p-values #if str($target_db.db_source) == 'cached' #set $db_path = $target_db.db.fields.db_path #set $ctrl_db_path = $target_db.db.fields.ctrl_db #else #if $target_db.genome_fasta.is_of_type('fasta.gz') gunzip -c '$target_db.genome_fasta' > genome.fna && #else ln -s '$target_db.genome_fasta' genome.fna && #end if MakeUserDB.sh genome.fna USER_DB > /dev/null && MakeUserShuffledDB.sh genome.fna USER_SHUFFLED_DB > /dev/null && #set $db_path = 'USER_DB/genome.fna' #set $ctrl_db_path = 'USER_SHUFFLED_DB/genome.fna' #end if
## the effective database size used for the BLAST statistics and the p-values: taken from the ## data table, from the user, or, if no size is given, the number of bases of the database #if str($target_db.db_source) == 'cached' DBSIZE=$target_db.db.fields.dbsize && #elif str($target_db.dbsize) != 'None' DBSIZE=$target_db.dbsize && #else DBSIZE=\$(awk '!/^>/ {n += length($0)} END {print n}' genome.fna) && #end if
#set $pam_option = '-pam_search_' + str($scoring.pam_search)
#if str($spacer_input.input_type) == 'fasta' ## CRISPRTarget.pl only accepts array annotations, therefore the individual ## steps it performs are run here: the search in the target and in the control ## database, the scoring, and the rendering of the reports mkdir -p out && CRISPRTarget_cmd.pl -fasta spacers.fna -db '$db_path' -bed_indexed_fna '$db_path' -dbsize "\${DBSIZE}" -evalue $blast.evalue -gapopen $blast.gapopen -gapextend $blast.gapextend -reward $blast.reward -penalty $blast.penalty -word_size $blast.word_size -cpu "\${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1}" -nr -no_acc_parsing -parse_acc_from_desc -out out/main && CRISPRTarget_cmd.pl -fasta spacers.fna -db '$ctrl_db_path' -bed_indexed_fna '$ctrl_db_path' -dbsize "\${DBSIZE}" -evalue $blast.evalue -gapopen $blast.gapopen -gapextend $blast.gapextend -reward $blast.reward -penalty $blast.penalty -word_size $blast.word_size -cpu "\${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1}" -nr -no_acc_parsing -out out/ctrl && PAMRescore.pl -tab out/main/input_array_report.pam.txt -tab_neg out/ctrl/input_array_report.pam.txt -out out/input_array_report.tab.txt -min_score $scoring.min_score -compute_pval -guess_url $pam_option && CRISPRTargetGraphics.pl -in out/input_array_report.tab.txt -txt out/input_array_report.txt -include_url -include_pvalue && CRISPRTargetGraphics.pl -in out/input_array_report.tab.txt -html out/input_array_report.html -include_url -include_pvalue #else ## CRISPRTarget.pl runs all steps of the analysis CRISPRTarget.pl -gff spacers.gff -db '$db_path' -ctrl_db '$ctrl_db_path' -dbsize "\${DBSIZE}" -evalue $blast.evalue -gapopen $blast.gapopen -gapextend $blast.gapextend -reward $blast.reward -penalty $blast.penalty -word_size $blast.word_size -cpu "\${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1}" -min_score $scoring.min_score $pam_option -out out && ## CRISPRTarget.pl reports errors without setting a non-zero exit code test -e out/input_array_report.html #end if

param.name: input_type
param.label: Spacer input
param.help: Spacers can be provided as CRISPR array annotation in CRISPRDetect GFF format (which also contains the repeat sequences and the array types) or as a plain FASTA file of spacer sequences.

param.name: crispr_gff
param.label: CRISPR array annotation in CRISPRDetect GFF format

param.name: db_source
param.label: Target database
param.help: Databases configured by the Galaxy administrator are pre-indexed and come with a suitable shuffled database for the p-value estimation.
param.option: Use a database configured by the administrator
Build a database from a FASTA file in the history

param.name: db
param.label: Target database with shuffled control database

validator.message: No CRISPRTarget database is configured, contact the Galaxy administrator.

param.name: genome_fasta
param.label: Target sequences (e.g. phage or plasmid genomes)

param.name: dbsize
param.label: Effective database size
param.help: Used for the BLAST statistics and for the p-values. If left empty, the actual size of the database (the total number of bases in the FASTA file) is used. Give a fixed value, e.g. the 1000000000 suggested by CRISPRTarget, to obtain p-values that can be compared between databases of different sizes. Note that the database is rebuilt for every run, use the CRISPRTarget make database tool if you need the database repeatedly.

param.name: min_score
param.label: Minimum score of reported targets
param.help: The score is the sum of the weights of the matches, mismatches and PAMs of the spacer/target alignment (see Biswas et al. 2013 for details).

param.name: pam_search
param.label: PAM search
param.help: Restricting the search to the PAMs of the CRISPR super-type or of the CRISPR type requires that the type of the array is known, i.e. that the annotation contains it. Searching all PAMs is the safe choice.
param.option: Search PAMs of the same CRISPR super-type
Search PAMs of the exact CRISPR type

param.label: Word size
param.help: 7 is the word size for short queries that CRISPRTarget uses

tool.help:
**What it does**
CRISPRTarget predicts the targets of CRISPR spacers in a sequence database. Spacers are matched to the database with BLASTN and the hits are scored with a model that takes the number and the distribution of mismatches, the PAM (protospacer adjacent motif) and the flanks of the match into account (see Biswas et al. 2013). The score of a match is compared to the scores obtained with a shuffled version of the database to compute a p-value.
The tool reports the predicted targets in three formats:
- a **tabular** file with one line per predicted target, - a **text** report with the spacer/target alignments, and - an **html** report with the same content as the text report.
Spacers can be given as CRISPR array annotation in CRISPRDetect GFF format or as FASTA file of spacer sequences. In the former case the repeat sequences and, if available, the CRISPR types are taken from the annotation. For plain spacer sequences only the search over all known PAMs is meaningful.
-----
**Databases**
@DATABASE_HELP@
FASTA files of pre-built databases are available from Zenodo and can be turned into a database with the CRISPRTarget make database tool:
- phage: https://zenodo.org/records/24148305/files/phage.fa.zip - plasmid: https://zenodo.org/records/24148305/files/plasmid.fa.zip - vhdb (small test database): https://zenodo.org/records/21869551/files/all_vhdb_full.fna.zip
The much larger (~250 GB uncompressed, about 500 GB of disk space including the BLAST database) MetaVR database can be obtained from https://www.meta-virome.org/Downloads (see also the instructions in the README of the CRISPRTarget repository).
-----
**Output columns**
The tabular output contains one line per spacer/target match with the following columns:
- ``Spacer_accession`` - accession of the sequence the CRISPR array was found in - ``Spacer_ID`` - identifier of the spacer - ``Target_accession`` - accession of the database sequence the spacer matches - ``Target_start``, ``Target_end`` - start and end of the match in the target sequence - ``Target_flank_3p``, ``Target_flank_5p`` - flanks of the match in the target sequence - ``Target_score`` - score of the match - ``Target_strand`` - strand of the target sequence the spacer matches - ``PAM_3p_seq_plus_strand``, ``PAM_5p_seq_plus_strand``, ``PAM_3p_seq_minus_strand``, ``PAM_5p_seq_minus_strand`` - PAM candidates found next to the match - ``Potential_self_match`` - the spacer matches a sequence flanking its own array - ``Spacer_seq``, ``Target_seq`` - spacer sequence (RNA alphabet) and the target sequence it matches - ``Spacer_description``, ``Target_description`` - descriptions of the spacer and the target sequence - ``URL_Link`` - link to the match in the NCBI sequence viewer - ``Spacer_flank_5p``, ``Spacer_flank_3p`` - flanks of the spacer in the CRISPR array - ``CRISPR_type`` - CRISPR type of the array (if known) - ``Repeat_seq`` - repeat sequence of the array - ``PAM_type_5p_plus_strand``, ``PAM_type_5p_minus_strand``, ``PAM_type_3p_plus_strand``, ``PAM_type_3p_minus_strand`` - types of the PAMs found next to the match - ``P_value`` - p-value of the score, estimated from the shuffled control database - ``Source_spacer_flank_3p``, ``Source_spacer_flank_5p``, ``Source_target_flank_3p``, ``Source_target_flank_5p`` - flanks of the spacer and of the target in the source sequences - ``Flank_match`` - the spacer and the target flanks are matching - ``Legacy_score`` - score of the web version of CRISPRTarget
-----
**Example**
Searching the array annotation of *Streptococcus pyogenes* NC_002737 in a database of phage genomes reports e.g. the spacer ``NC_002737_2_2|860921_860951`` matching position 1101-1130 of *Streptococcus* phage Javan484 with a score of 30 and a 3' PAM (CTT) on the minus strand.
